note: Merged from eight batch files, each scored by its own independent agent.

scores.notes: Moses at left foreground extends staff over the parted sea while Israelites walk the dry path between wave-walls; God appears only as a fiery cloud column at top center with no face or human shape. Painting reaches all four edges and no lettering in corners.

Both seraphim (upper left and upper right) have only two wings each, with none covering face or feet, and both hold tongs with live coals (the later verse 6 moment) instead of the six-winged pose the verse describes. The throne at center is empty with smoke and fire only, so God gets no figure. Edges are full and no lettering is visible.

Gouache-like painting reaching all four borders: flock mostly lying in green grass (lower left/centre), shepherd in undyed cloak with staff (right), still pool, low stone walls and village (upper right), misty sunrise. No lettering in corners or sky.

Engraving: the Ancient of Days is only a white sunburst, cloud and a central column of flame (top and middle centre) with empty thrones and wheels, no face or figure in the light; Daniel looks up from a ledge at lower left while white-robed attendants fill the plain to the horizon. Painting reaches all four edges and no lettering anywhere, including the scroll case at Daniel's hip.

Empty white throne under a rainbow and cloud radiance at center with no figure for God; lion, ox, winged man and eagle stand on a reflective tiled floor. Only the lion (left) is covered in eyes and the 'sea of glass' reads as a glossy tile floor, so the verse is only partly depicted; edges painted to all borders.

A handwriting-like scribble resembling a signature is scratched into the paving stone at bottom center (about x 670-760, y 715-750). The empty doorway with plain scrolls, jar and mat is right, but it is an oblique view under a bright midday blue sky rather than a frontal doorway view in late golden light.

Realist oil painted to all edges: crowded flock resting (lower left), shepherd with staff (centre) in olive tunic and brown cloak, still pool (right), village with low stone walls on the hill, mist and sunrise glow upper left. No text found; flock overlaps read as occlusion.

Moses at left holds two separate staffs at once, a straight one planted in his left hand and a crook-topped one raised in his right, which is contradictory. God appears only as a distant thin pillar of fire and smoke at top centre with no figure; edges are fully painted and no text.

The tied scroll held by two hands at center is covered in dark glyph-like script along its outer wrapping. Village street with passers-by at left and a Roman soldier at right matches the scene; a small cross/antenna-like mark sits on a rooftop just left of the scroll top.

Kneeling soldiers cast lots over a spread tunic, with Jesus crucified on the center cross, spears, a bundle and the city walls all as requested. The small titulus plaque at the top of the center cross (top center-left) carries a faint row of dark letter-like marks; the plaque on the left cross looks blank.

Engraving reaching all edges; God absent (smoke-filled sanctuary, no figure). The right seraph holds tongs with a live coal (the verse 6 moment) while its feet are bare and only about four wings show; the left seraph alone has the six-wing face/feet covering, so two moments are mixed above the bowed Isaiah.

The Ancient of Days is only a white swirling radiance with fireballs and flying burning wheels in the sky (top centre to right), no figure. But the attendants in the middle ground are obvious copy-pasted clones (same curly-haired bearded man in the same stride repeated in a line) walking past plain empty stone seats on a daylit plain, so the heavenly court reads mundane and artificial; edges full, no text.

Jesus at center faces the viewer with his back to the tomb, hand raised skyward, while a bearded long-haired man who looks like a second Jesus already stands upright in an ordinary tunic inside the tomb doorway (right), so the call and the not-yet-emerged, grave-bound Lazarus conflict. Crowd with children crowds close at left rather than at a distance; edges full, no text.

The throne at center is empty, with only radiance, cloud, lightning and a rainbow, so God gets no figure. The winged lion (left) has four lion legs plus a robed standing body that drops into the water, and the eagle (right) is likewise robed like a person. All four creatures wade knee-deep in a wavy sea instead of standing by a crystal glass sea, and their eyes appear only on the wings and stoles.

Engraving printed as a plate: white paper margins with a ruled border on the left, right and bottom. Signature-like initials sit in the bottom-left and bottom-right corners, with a small glyph near bottom centre. God is shown only as radiance through cloud (top centre). The water is rolling rather than still.

Tinted engraving: the father runs in from the right foreground with arms outstretched and cloak flying toward the son standing on the winding road at left, beside a low stone wall, olive trees and distant village. Hatching reaches all four edges and no lettering in any corner.

Light breaks through clouds at upper center over a dark, still expanse of water reflecting a band of light; zoomed clouds show no face or figure. Dark painted strokes reach all four edges; no marks in corners.

Jesus (center) cries out with his arm raised beside the open tomb and rolled stone, with Martha bowed at left and the crowd at right. He faces right toward the crowd and sky rather than toward the dark tomb mouth behind him at left. Edges are full, the corners are clean and there is no lettering.

Engraving reaches all four edges; light breaks through cloud over dark still water with no figure in the glow. Legible signature lettering sits in both bottom corners ('VABSCAP'-like script at bottom right, a scrawl at bottom left).

Father in brown cloak lunges in from the right foreground with arms wide toward the travel-worn son (frayed hem, satchel) standing on the dirt road at left, stone wall and olive trees between; only these two figures. Light reads as bright day rather than dusk and a columned temple sits on the far hill (top right), minor; paint reaches all edges and no text.

Foreground hands hold an opened two-roller scroll with a blank papyrus sheet over a table, with a second red-wrapped roller beside it, instead of the requested closed scroll with a title wrapping. Square with temple-like building, passers-by at left and Roman soldier at right fits; edges full, no lettering visible.

Four soldiers kneel around a spread tunic casting dice, with a spear and shield against a rock and Jesus crucified at upper right before the city walls, which matches well. The titulus board at the top of the cross (about x 930-990, y 25-45) shows clear glyph-like scribbled marks.

Fresco-like painting reaching all edges, with no figure in the smoke cloud (God absent). The left seraph holds tongs with a burning coal (the verse 6 moment) over the bowed Isaiah. Both seraphim show only about four wings and bare uncovered feet, so the verse 2 wing posture is missing and two moments are mixed.

In the court at centre right a white-haired, white-bearded man in a white robe sits enthroned (with a second seated elder left of the empty central throne), which reads as the Ancient of Days given a human body; faint human figures also stand in the clouds at upper left. Edges fully painted and no text.

Roman soldiers kneel around a spread tunic casting lots in the foreground with Jesus crucified at upper right and Jerusalem's walls at left, matching the scene. The small pale title board on the cross (top right) carries dark slanted glyph-like strokes that read as an inscription; edges painted full.

The engraving sits on a cream paper plate, with a ruled border line and a blank margin on all four sides. The titulus at the top of the cross (about x 870-910, y 40-65) is filled with scratchy letter-like marks. The scene itself fits: three soldiers point at dice on a spread tunic, with a spear and shield against a rock, Jesus on the cross and the city beyond.

Opaque gouache with a ragged white unpainted paper border on all four sides (a margin, not an ink-and-watercolor fade). The scene itself fits: foreground hands set a tied, unlettered scroll on a wooden stand, with passers-by, a pedimented synagogue and a Roman soldier on the road at right.

Jesus stands beside the open rock tomb with the round stone rolled aside (left), mouth open and right arm raised, Martha beside him with head bowed and hands clasped, villagers gathered on the path at right. He faces up and away to the right rather than toward the dark opening, so the call reads aimed at the sky, but nothing is wrong or contradictory; edges full, no text.

Empty mudbrick courtyard with a lit doorway holding a shelf of plain rolled scrolls (center), a clay jar and rolled woven mat at lower left, no people. Scroll ends are blank on zoom, no corner marks, and painting reaches all four edges.

The sea is not divided: low breaking waves leave only a narrow wet gap at center, with no standing walls of water and no dry sea floor, so the verse's central miracle is missing. Moses stands at center-right with his staff over the waves while Israelites crowd the left. God appears only as a flame-and-cloud plume on the horizon at top center, and a walled city sits on the far shore at upper right.

Painting reaches all edges, with an empty jeweled throne under a starburst and green rainbow (no God figure) and a glassy floor. The creatures are malformed: the lion (left) wears a red stole and white shirt over its forelegs, and the eagle's (right) body turns into a red-and-white skirt with talons below. Eyes appear only on the wings, not over the bodies.

The scroll at centre is unrolled on a lectern and covered in hieroglyph-like glyphs, with a cord knotted across its open face (both open and tied shut), instead of a closed scroll. Passers-by at left and a Roman soldier at right are as requested; edges full.

David stands at left with the sling hanging from his hand while armored Goliath topples forward face-down mid-ground right, spear flying; Israelites watch from the upper-left ridge and a Philistine shield line stands at upper right. Goliath is not drawn at giant scale, but no lettering appears and paint reaches all four edges.

This is a frontal view of the empty open doorway of a mudbrick and stone house, with tied closed scrolls on a low shelf inside, a clay jar and a woven mat in the courtyard, and a golden evening sky at upper right. There are no figures and no lettering, the scrolls are blank and all edges are fully painted.

Tinted engraving with hatching to all four edges: shepherd in an undyed cloak leaning on a staff (left-centre), many sheep lying in the grass, a still pool behind a low dry-stone wall (right), mist and a hill village at sunrise. No lettering in corners or sky.

The scroll held on the lectern at centre is unrolled showing columns of small writing, with a ribbon tied in a bow across the open sheet, rather than a closed scroll. Square, synagogue-like building with steps, passers-by and a Roman soldier with spear (right) match; edges full.

A cursive signature-like inscription is written in the bottom-right corner. Goliath (right) falls sideways with his face turned up toward the viewer rather than on his face, while David stands at left with the sling.

The younger son appears twice: a ragged young man stands in the right foreground, and a small figure in the same grey cloak, tunic and satchel stands far down the road at center (about x 760-815, y 350-485). This duplicates the son across two moments. The father runs in from the left with arms outstretched, and a large white colonnaded temple-like building sits at upper right.

Painting reaches all edges. Contradictory state: David's sling (lower left) still holds a stone with motion lines while Goliath is already toppling (right), and the stone by Goliath's head hangs below his helmeted face rather than sinking into his forehead. David stands square to the viewer instead of following through; the Philistines on the right ridge are in Roman-style armour.

The moment is contradictory: a stone is still in flight at centre and another sits in David's sling pouch (left), yet Goliath (right) is already struck with an impact flash at his brow and is falling backward rather than on his face; he also has two spears, one long one held diagonally and a second spearhead crossing behind his raised arm. Battle lines on both sides as requested; hatching reaches all edges and no text.

Sepia engraving of an empty courtyard with a clay jar at left-center, a woven mat along the bottom and an open doorway (center right) showing plain rolled scrolls on a shelf, two more lying on the floor; warm light falls across the threshold. Hatching runs to all four edges with no rule line, and no lettering or initials in corners or on scrolls.

Golden light breaks through clouds at top center and shines across dark green-and-umber waters filling the lower half, with no face, figure or shape in the clouds or the light. The paint reaches all four borders, with only slight edge darkening and no band, and there is no lettering or signature in any corner.
